messages.content: tell a story about two people who do not understand each other at first, then ask a question to help.

a man was moving things in his kitchen when his sister came to visit. he asked if she could bring the little chair from the living room. she came back with a small table instead. he looked at it and said he had asked for a chair. she said she had not been sure what he said over the sound of the radio. they chose to turn the radio off for a while. she asked which chair he would like, and he said the one by the window. this time she found the right one. they put it in the kitchen next to the table. then he made tea, and she sat on the chair while they talked. they had a laugh about the little table before going to turn the radio back on.
did she bring the right thing at first?
no. she brought a little table instead of a chair.
what helped her find the right chair?
she asked which chair he would like, and he said the one by the window.
write a story about a house in the morning and in the evening. keep the same family in it.

in the morning, a mother and her daughter sat in the kitchen of their little house. the mother made breakfast while the daughter put a book in her bag. after they ate, they put their cups on the kitchen table and left for school and work. the house was quiet while they were away. in the evening, they came back with a bag of food. the daughter put her book on the table and helped wash a tomato for dinner. her mother opened the kitchen window while she cooked. after dinner, they sat together and read from the book. the house was still little, and the kitchen was the same room, but now there was time to sit instead of getting ready to go.
was it a new family in the evening?
no. it was the same mother and daughter coming home.
what did the daughter put on the table in the evening?
her book.
tell a story about a boy waiting for his friend. his friend comes at the end.

a boy put a game on the table and sat by the window. his friend was coming to play, but was not there. after looking outside for a while, the boy took out some paper and a pencil. he started drawing a picture of the street. he drew the shop, the tree, and the little wall by his house. each time he looked outside, he found another thing to add. after a while, his father asked if he was still waiting. the boy said yes, but he was also making a picture. then there was a voice at the door. his friend had come with a book about a game. the boy put his picture on the shelf, and they sat together at the table.
did he only look outside while he waited?
no. he also drew a picture of the street.
did he put the picture away before his friend came?
no. he put it on the shelf after his friend came.
write a story about a woman who has little food ready when a friend visits. make it kind.

a woman opened the door to her friend, who had come after a long walk. the woman said she had not made a meal and only had bread, butter, and some apples. her friend said that was enough for her. they took the bread to the table, cut an apple, and made tea. at first, the woman kept saying she was sorry there was not more. her friend said she had come to see her, not to have a large dinner. then the woman sat down too. they took their time eating and talked about the walk. when they finished their tea, they made more and sat at the table again. the simple food had helped them start a visit, but the visit was about being together.
was the friend sad about there not being more food?
no. she said the food was enough and that she had come to see her friend.
what did they have with the bread?
butter, apple, and tea.
write a story about a girl finding a quiet place to read in a busy house.

a girl opened her book in the living room, but her brother was playing a game there. she tried the kitchen next, where her father was making dinner and talking on the phone. then she went to her bedroom and found her sister drawing on the bed. she asked if they could share the room and keep it quiet for a while. her sister said yes. the girl sat by the window with her book, and her sister kept drawing. both could stay in the room. after a while, the sister asked about the story. the girl finished the line she was reading, then talked about the boy in the book. they started looking at the picture on the page together.
did she have to make her sister leave?
no. they chose to share the room and keep it quiet.
where did she sit with her book?
by the bedroom window.
tell a story about a child learning to wait for an answer.

a child asked his grandmother what she did when she was little. before she could answer, he asked another question about her house. then he asked about her school. she said she would be happy to tell him, but she would need time to answer one question first. the child sat back in his chair. she started with the house, which had been her home as a child. he listened while she talked about the garden and the little kitchen where her family ate together. when she finished, he asked about her school again. this time, he waited. she said there was a story about a lost book she could tell him. he was happy that giving her time had helped him hear more.
did asking many things at once give him more of a story right away?
no. he had to give his grandmother time to answer.
what did she talk about first?
the house which had been her home as a child.
write a story about a box on a shelf. no one knows what is in it at first.

a brother and sister found a small box on a shelf in the room of their grandfather. the boy said there might be coins inside. the girl said there might be a photo. they asked their grandfather if they could open it. he said yes, and took it down for them. inside was a letter and a little key. the letter was from his sister, who had a home in another town. the key was for another small box from his sister. the children asked if the other box had coins in it. their grandfather said they could ask about that another day. for now, he would like to read the letter with them. they sat down and listened to the words of his sister.
did the children know what was in the box before opening it?
no. they were only saying what might be inside.
were there coins in that box?
no. there was a letter and a little key.
tell a story about someone who takes a break from writing and then starts again.

a woman sat with her paper and pen for a long time. she had started a letter, but could not think of what to say next. she put the pen down and went to the kitchen for water. while she drank, she looked out at the garden. a bird was standing on the wall with a leaf near its feet. she watched it for a little while, then went back to the table. the letter did not have to say everything at once. she wrote about the bird and the quiet afternoon. then she asked her friend how things were in the garden at her house. when she finished, she read the letter once and put it in her bag to send later.
did she stop writing for the rest of the day?
no. she took a break and then came back to finish it.
what did she look at during the break?
a bird on the garden wall.
write a story about two children who both want to use one book.

two children both asked for the same book on a table. one would like to read the story, and the other would like to look at each picture. they could not both hold it on their own at the same time. their father asked if they could sit together, but one child said he would like some quiet time with it. the other said that was okay if she could have it after. they chose to let him read first while she drew a picture. when he finished, he gave her the book. she looked at each picture, then asked him what was happening on one page. he sat down next to her and read that part to her. they had found time to use the book alone and together.
did they need another book to fix the problem?
no. one child had it first, and the other had it after.
who had it first?
the child who would like to read the story had it first.
tell a story about a man writing the wrong day in a note and fixing it before he sends it.

a man wrote a note asking his brother to come for lunch tomorrow. before he sent it, he looked at his plan for the day. tomorrow he would be away at work, and the day after tomorrow was free. he read the note again and saw that it had the wrong day. he did not send it as it was. instead, he wrote a new note asking his brother to come the day after tomorrow. he also said they could go for a walk after lunch if the weather was good. then he took one more look at the day. this time it was right. he sent the note and put the paper with his plan on the table, where he could see it in the morning.
did his brother get the note with the wrong day?
no. the man fixed it before he sent it.
when did he ask his brother to come?
the day after tomorrow.
write a story about someone finding a broken cup and asking about it before saying who did it.

a woman went into the kitchen and saw a broken cup on the floor. her son was standing by the door, but she did not say he had broken it. she asked what had been happening in the kitchen. he said his sister had tried to move the cup, but it had come off the table. his sister came in and said yes, she had tried to carry it and it broke. the woman asked both children to stay away from the broken cup while she cleaned the floor. after that, she put the other cups in the middle of the table. the boy brought a towel so she could finish cleaning. when the floor was ready, they sat down with a glass of water each and talked about the day.
did standing by the door mean the boy broke the cup?
no. being there did not tell the woman who broke it.
where did she put the other cups?
in the middle of the table.
tell a story about a child choosing how to spend time with a quiet friend.

a boy asked his friend if she would like to play a game. she said not right now. he asked if she would like to go outside, and she said she would like to stay in. then he looked at the book in her hand and asked what she was reading. she opened it to a picture of a bird and said she was learning about birds in the garden. he sat next to her, and they looked at the page together. after a while, they went to the window to see if a bird was outside. there was one on the wall. they did not need a game to have a good afternoon. looking at a book and then out of the window was enough.
did she want to play a game at first?
no. she said not right now.
what helped them find a thing to enjoy together?
he asked about the book she was reading.
write a story about a little table where someone works in the morning and has tea later.

a woman had a small table by her window. in the morning, she put her paper and pen on it and wrote a letter. when she finished, she moved the paper to a shelf and put the pen in a box. her sister came to visit in the afternoon. the woman brought two cups of tea and put them on the same table. they sat on each side and looked at the garden while they talked. her sister asked where she did her writing. the woman said she had done it at the table between them. she could use a small place for many things. it just had to have room for the thing she was doing at that time.
did she get another table for tea?
no. she had tea at the same little table by the window.
where did the paper go after she finished writing?
on a shelf.
tell a story about a girl choosing another chair after trying to read in the first one.

a girl went into the library and saw a chair by a large window. she chose it because she could see a tree outside. when she sat down with her book, people kept walking by on the way to the door. it was hard to keep reading. she looked around and found another chair by a small table at the back of the room. there was still light, but people were not walking by it. she moved her book and bag to that chair. now she could read for a while. before going home, she looked out of the large window once more. she still could enjoy the tree, even after choosing a quiet place away from it.
did she say she did not like the tree after that?
no. she could still enjoy the tree, but she chose a quiet place to read.
why did she move?
people kept walking by the first chair, which made reading hard.
write a story about a child who gets water on the floor and asks a parent for help.

a child was carrying water to the table when some of it went on the floor. he looked at the water and then at his father, who was reading in the living room. the child could have walked away, but he called his father instead. he said there was water on the floor and he did not know which towel to use. his father came to the kitchen and gave him a clean towel. they cleaned the floor together. then his father asked him to try holding the glass with both hands while carrying it. the child tried again with a little water in the glass. this time he got to the table and put it down. he was happy he had asked for help.
did the child walk away and leave the water on the floor?
no. he called his father and asked for help.
what did he learn about carrying the glass?
to hold it with both hands.
tell a quiet story about two friends who only have a little time to meet.

two friends had been trying to find a free afternoon together. one worked in a shop, and the other had to be home when her children came from school. they could not find a long time that worked for both of them. then one asked if they could meet for a short walk after lunch. they met by the library and walked to the little shop at the end of the street. on the way, they talked about their family and a book they both knew. before going home, they sat for a little while by a tree. the visit was short, but both were happy they had made time. they did not have to wait for a free day to see each other.
did they have the afternoon free for a long visit?
no. they had a short walk after lunch.
were they still happy to meet?
yes. even a short visit gave them time together.
write a story about a father asking about a picture his daughter made. he does not know what it is.

a father found a picture on the kitchen table. there was a large green shape, a blue line, and a little yellow circle. he did not know if it was a tree, water, and the sun, so he asked his daughter to tell him about it. she said the green shape was a house for birds, the blue line was a road, and the yellow circle was a ball. he sat next to her and asked who would play with the ball. she said the birds could use it in her story. the picture did not have to be the same as the world outside. he listened while she talked about the world she was making on paper.
was the yellow circle the sun?
no. in her picture, it was a ball.
how did her father find that out?
he asked her to tell him about the picture.
tell a story about a woman who has a new free morning at home after her plan changes.

a woman was ready to leave for a visit when her friend called. the friend had to go to work and asked if they could meet another day. the woman said yes and put her bag down. at first she did not know what to do with the free morning. then she saw the book she had left on the sofa. she opened the window, made tea, and sat down to read. after a while, she took her cup to the kitchen and washed it. she still had time before lunch, so she went into the garden for a short walk. the morning had changed, but it had room for quiet things she could enjoy.
did she still go to visit her friend that morning?
no. they chose to meet another day.
what did she do before going into the garden?
she read, took her cup to the kitchen, and washed it.
write a story about a brother asking before moving the work his sister left on the table.

a boy came to the table with a plate of food. his sister had left paper and a pencil in the middle of the table. he would need space, but he did not know if the paper was ready to move. he called to ask her. she came from the bedroom and said the picture was not finished. she put the pencil in a box and carried the paper to her desk. then she asked if he would like her to sit with him while he ate. he said yes, and she brought her own cup to the table. there was space for both of them now. she was happy he had asked before moving the picture, and he was happy to have someone to talk to over lunch.
did he move the paper before asking her?
no. he asked first, and she moved it to her desk.
was the picture finished?
no. she said it was not finished.
tell a story about a child learning to write a letter by hand. do not make all the writing easy to read right away.

a child sat at the table with paper and a pen. she would like to write to her aunt, but her first line went too close to the side of the paper. she started again on another piece. this time, she took her time and left more space. some words were still hard to read. her mother sat next to her and asked what she would like the letter to say. together, they read the words she had already put down. the child chose one sentence to try again. it was easy enough for her to read back to her mother. she had not finished the letter, but now she knew which sentence she could write next.
was all the writing easy to read at once?
no. some words were hard to read, and she was still learning.
had she finished by the end of the story?
no. she had made a start and knew what to try next.
